kits.name: OPEN SOURCE STARTER
kits.summary: A minimal repository skeleton: license, contribution rules, conduct, security policy, issue and PR templates, and agent instructions.
kits.description: Start a public repository with the documents contributors and agents expect. Choose one license from this kit, then replace the placeholders in the templates.
notes: MIT is a safe default; swap in Apache-2.0, GPL-3.0, or MPL-2.0 if the project needs different terms.
The DCO is optional if the project uses a CLA instead.

kits.name: AGENT-READY REPO
kits.summary: Instructions, tool definitions, evaluation criteria, and contribution rules for repositories that coding agents will work in.
kits.description: Make a repository legible to coding agents without giving them uncontrolled access. The kit pairs concrete commands and boundaries with honest evaluation and disclosure rules.
notes: Fill AGENTS.md from the actual repository; do not copy commands that do not work.
Keep MCP permissions read-only unless a task requires writes.
Review the evaluation checklist before trusting an agent with releases or credentials.

kits.name: WEBSITE POLICY PACK
kits.summary: Privacy, cookies, terms, accessibility, acceptable use, DMCA, and security.txt templates for a public website or app.
kits.description: A starting pack for a small public site. Every document is a template, not legal advice; adapt it to the jurisdiction, data flows, and platform that actually apply.
notes: Remove sections that do not describe your actual data practices.
Have the final documents reviewed before relying on them.

kits.name: LICENSE PACK
kits.summary: Common license texts, source headers, and an open-source notices template in one download.
kits.description: A compact set for projects that need a license, consistent source headers, and a notices file. Pick one license; the others are included for comparison.
notes: Do not apply multiple incompatible licenses to the same code.
Keep the copyright notice and license text with every distribution.
Use the SPDX identifiers in source headers where the project supports them.
